content: KMC partitions k-mers into disk buckets via signatures (a filtered subset of canonical minimizers). Canonical-aware selection takes min(m-mer, revcomp(m-mer)) so a k-mer and its reverse complement always share a bucket; otherwise counts split. KMC2 signature rules exclude m-mers starting AAA/ACA or containing internal AA to avoid low-complexity mega-buckets (~11% smaller super-k-mer volume vs plain minimizers). Two phases: distribute super-k-mers (runs of consecutive k-mers sharing a signature) to bucket files sized to fit RAM, then sort/count each bucket independently (radix sort). KMC3 samples input to build a signature-frequency histogram and packs signatures into a capped number of bins (~2000). Sources: IJC 2020 GPU super-k-mer paper, WABI 2022 LIPIcs vol242, PMC6280066 benchmark study, KMC3 thesis (uniba.sk).
